<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. V.|ACCORDING TO S. MARKE.|99}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=5|verse=21}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 9, 18. Luc. 8, 42.''}}* And vvhen {{sc|Iesvs}} had passed in boate againe ouer the straite, a great multitude assembled together vnto him, and he vvas about the sea. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=22}}† And there commeth one of the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''Archsynagogue'', cheefe gouerner of a Synagogue.}}∷ Archsynagogs, named Iaîrus: and seeing him, he falleth dovvne at his feete, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=23}}† and besought him much, saying, That my daughter is at the point of death, come, impose thy hands vpon her, that she may be safe and liue. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=24}}† And he vvent vvith him, and a great multitude folovved him, and they thronged him.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=25}}† And a vvoman vvhich vvas in an issue of bloud tvvelue yeres, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=26}}† and had suffred many things of many Physicions, and had bestovved al that she had, neither vvas any thing the better, but vvas rather vvorse: {{verse|chapter=5|verse=27}}† vvhen she had heard of {{sc|Iesvs}}, she came in the preasse behind him, and touched his garment. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=28}}† for she said, That {{sup|‖}} if I shal touche but his garment, I shal be safe. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=29}}† And forthvvith the fountaine of her bloud vvas dried: and she felt in her body that she vvas healed of the maladie. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=30}}† And immediatly {{sc|Iesvs}} knovving in him self the {{sup|‖}} vertue that had proceeded from him, turning to the multitude, said, Who hath touched my garments? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=31}}† And his Disciples said to him, Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who hath touched me? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=32}}† And he looked about to see her that had done this. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=33}}† But the vvoman fearing and trembling, knovving vvhat vvas done in her: came and fel dovvne before him, and told him al the truth. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=34}}† And he said to her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee safe, goe in peace, and be vvhole of thy maladie.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=35}}† As he vvas yet speaking, they come {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`from''}}`to' the Archsynagogue, saying, That thy daughter is dead: vvhy doest thou trouble the Maister any further? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=36}}† But {{sc|Iesvs}} hauing heard the vvord that vvas spoken, saith to the Archsynagogue, Feare not: {{sup|‖}} only beleeue. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=37}}† And he admitted not any man to folovv him, but Peter and Iames and Iohn the brother of Iames. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=38}}† And they come to the Archsynagogs house, and he seeth a tumult, and folke vveeping and vvailing much. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=39}}† And going in, he saith to them: Why make you this a doe and vveepe? the vvenche is not dead, but {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ To Christ, that can more easily raise a dead man then we can doe one that is but a sleepe, death is but sleepe. ''Aug. de verb. Do. Ser. 44''.}}∷ sleepeth. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=40}}† And they derided him. But he hauing put forth al, taketh the father and the mother of the vvenche, and them that vvere vvith him, and they goe in vvhere the vvenche vvas lying. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=41}}† And holding the vvenches hand, he saith to her, ''Talitha cumi'', vvhich is being interpreted, {{sup|‖}} ''wenche'' (I say to thee) ''arise''. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=42}}† and {{hws|forth|forthvvith}}<noinclude>{{rh||N ij|vvith}}</noinclude>
